area: Benchmarking, validation, calibration, and test coverage (datagen + tests + tools/verify_data.py) — assessed for what a traffic/comm REALISM benchmark harness would need
current_state:
ALL existing benchmarking is detection/ML-quality oriented; realism measurement is limited to one GNSS-error calibration and a 5-row plausibility scorecard. Details:

1) src/scms_sim_ref/datagen/benchmark.py — pure-numpy ML detection benchmark over ml/*.{parquet,csv} tables. Metrics: tie-averaged Mann-Whitney ROC-AUC (:83-95), PR-AUC (:98-110), precision/recall/F1/balanced-accuracy at 0.5 (:113-124), best-F1 operating point (:127-145), recall@1%FPR "the operating point a real MA cares about" (:180-187), seeded percentile-bootstrap 95% CI (:148-165). Baselines: numpy logistic regression (:61-80) + numpy GBDT via datagen/models.py fit_gbdt (:225-232). Tasks in run() (:382-421): subject_is_attacker, report_is_true_detection, vehicle_is_attacker (oracle linkage = upper bound, :395), vehicle_is_attacker_ma_linked (:397-400), MA linkage purity (:364-379), leave-one-attack-family-out novel-attack AUC (:236-264), 1-hop graph message-passing baseline over graph_edges (:267-304), unsupervised one-class Mahalanobis on benign-only train (:307-334), leave-one-domain-out generalization (:337-361), temporal split forward-in-time (:407-411). EXCLUDED_FEATURE_COLUMNS frozenset (:32-35) is the single source of truth for the feature/label firewall.

2) src/scms_sim_ref/datagen/calibration.py — the ONLY quantitative calibration vs real-world references. It fits benign horizontal GNSS error from ground_truth/gt_emissions_sample.jsonl (:27-33, 55-59) by Rayleigh MLE and compares to a literature constant REF_CEP_M=2.5 m (:23-24) via a hand-rolled 1-sample KS statistic (:35-42); flags cep_in_real_range for 1.0–12.0 m (:66) and shape_is_rayleigh_like for KS<0.25 (:69); checks confidence calibration = empirical coverage of the broadcast 95% radius, "well_calibrated" band 0.85–0.985 (:72-83). Reference = hard-coded constants from literature, NOT external reference data files. Nothing else (speed, accel, headway, radio) is calibrated.

3) src/scms_sim_ref/datagen/validate.py — dataset-level detection metrics + leakage: lints every ma/*.jsonl row with the leakage linter (:27-34); revocation precision/recall with faulty-vs-benign false-revocation separation (:60-66, 118-136); detection latency onset→revocation median/p90/max (:42-59); recall_by_family and recall_by_type (:69-88); per-detector (reason-code) report-level precision + coverage (:92-116); RSU contribution stats (:97-116). CLI exits 1 on any leak (:140-150).

4) src/scms_sim_ref/datagen/leakage_linter.py — recursive forbidden-key scan find_forbidden_keys (:25-40) using schemas/records.is_forbidden_feature_key; assert_ma_visible rejects _visibility==ORACLE records (:51-63); lint_ma_dataset / lint_feature_frame batch variants (:65-80).

5) src/scms_sim_ref/datagen/corpus_report.py — read-only deterministic corpus balance/coverage report for datagen.massive corpora: class balance with thresholds MIN_CLASS_FRAC=0.02 and ATTACKER_BENIGN_BAND=(0.05,1.0) (:58-59, 117-173); attack family/type coverage measured against the code-derived KNOWN_ATTACK_TYPES space (:44-55, 176-235); domain diversity (topologies + event timelines, :238-264); difficulty spread = per-domain recall max-min >= 0.15 (:60, 267-303); size + domain-dominance factor 4.0 (:61, 306-367); CLI exits nonzero on warnings so it works as a CI gate (:564-565).

6) src/scms_sim_ref/datagen/datasheet.py — auto datasheet embedding validate+benchmark+calibration. Contains the qualitative "Realism scorecard (vs real-world reference ranges)" (:216-252): 5 wide range checks — median GNSS 95% confidence 2–20 m, benign speed p95 5–45 m/s, attacker prevalence 0.03–0.45, faulty prevalence 0–0.20, report FP rate 0–0.30 — plus the calibration CEP/KS/coverage lines (:236-251). A "Traffic flow & congestion" section (:172-205) reports peak concurrency, mean arrival rate, benign speed stats and queued(<5 m/s) fraction, and lists active realism features.

7) tools/verify_data.py — full data-CORRECTNESS audit over datasets/ (run in CI via tests/test_dataset_integrity.py): leakage/privacy L1-L3 (:96-120), referential integrity R1-R3 incl. RSU reporter allowance (:122-156), label correctness C1-C6 (:158-207, 404-417), count reconciliation CNT1-4 (:209-241), split integrity S1-S2 (:243-258), value sanity V1-V4 incl. attacker_pct plausibility and falsified-emission truth (:260-288, 419-441), sha256 file/aggregate digests I1-I2 (:290-321), graph integrity E3 with RSU-node regimes (:323-372), SCHEMA1 schema-vs-benchmark contract (:374-400), N1 world provenance = network.json node/edge index validity + custom_network count reconciliation (structural only, :443-489), VRU/DENM leakage+consistency VRU1/VRU2/DENM1/DENM2 (:491-624).

8) Integration points: campaign.py runs validate per-domain (:105-106) and benchmark on the merged set (:166-173); massive.py the same (:463, 559-563 writes merged_benchmark.json); foundry.py uses validate's recall/recall_by_family as evolutionary fitness with a report-activity validity gate (foundry.py:196-231); datasheet embeds everything.

9) tests/ + conftest.py: conftest only injects src/ on sys.path. ~50 test files, 8.5k lines. Realism-relevant coverage is DIRECTIONAL behavior assertions on the pure-Python engine, pinned by golden byte-digests (default digest 04ae9736f519… pinned in test_network_fidelity.py:33, test_lane_changes.py:19, test_gap_acceptance.py:24, test_radio_propagation.py:20): test_flow.py — IDM congestion spreads speeds (pstdev>1.5, :128-137), rush vs uniform demand CV (:148-164), fleet-class kinematics (:167-182), multilane relieves gridlock (:210-223), turn-slowdown corner dips (:226-243), lights create stops (:246-255), ring on-road fraction >0.95 (:258-273), grid extent bounds (:276-293), precision/recall floors under congestion (:62-70, 120-144); test_gap_acceptance.py — yield telemetry counts, "no through-each-other" conflict metric, no-deadlock throughput, precision preserved (:142-220); test_lane_changes.py — MOBIL transitions adjacent-lane only, benign heading transients 3–13 deg kept under the 35-deg detector threshold, precision preserved (:81-137); test_network_fidelity.py — signal-phase 2-colouring per topology, arterial/local speed tiers change kinematics measurably (:119-211); test_roads.py — gravity OD trip-length law, turn geometry; test_radio.py — range limits report volume, packet loss monotonicity, timing attacks (:16-28); test_radio_propagation.py — log-distance soft range heard-distance reconstruction from detnorm_acceptanceRangeThreshold (:58-72), sigma=0 collapses to disc byte-identically (:104-118), pathloss-exponent monotonicity (:128-140); test_realism.py — >=5 attack types, faulty class not revoked, benign false positives exist, CEP in range (:20-54); test_calibration.py — synthetic 2-D Gaussian recovers CEP and 95% coverage; 1-D radius bug flagged (:23-45); test_gui_realism.py — GUI curated realism knobs contract + "Max realism" preset validates (grid road, lane changes, gap acceptance, logdistance radio, lights, rush demand, VRUs) (:34-256); test_osm_import.py — OSM XML→CustomNetwork with maxspeed parsing and RDP simplification (offline synthetic fixture); test_custom_networks.py, test_massive_worlds.py — custom/spider topologies, event timelines, multi-topology corpora; test_end_to_end.py — generate→featurize→benchmark→calibration→datasheet→audit chain; test_dataset_integrity.py — verify_data audit over committed datasets as a build gate; plus VRU/DENM/RSU/attack/foundry/GUI suites.

10) MOSAIC layer (scms-sim/): no benchmark/validation harness at all — only scenario generators (gen_scenario.py, make_scms_*.ps1) and the Java apps (ScmsBeaconApp.java has a CBR-proxy channel-load drop model :110, :222-232). third_party/veremi-nextgen carries real MOSAIC/OMNeT++ configs (snirThreshold 4dB etc.) usable as reference configs, but nothing in-repo compares against them.
gaps: NO traffic-realism metrics exist anywhere: no fundamental diagram (flow-density-speed), no time-headway/gap distributions, no acceleration/jerk distributions, no travel-time/queue-length/stop-count statistics, no lane-change-rate comparison, no trip-length distribution vs real city data. Grep for fundamental/headway/wasserstein across src/ confirms only IDM's idm_time_headway parameter (run.py:431) and the GNSS KS statistic (calibration.py:35).

Calibration covers exactly ONE quantity (benign GNSS horizontal error vs a hard-coded Rayleigh CEP50=2.5 m constant, calibration.py:23-24). Nothing is calibrated against real traffic datasets (NGSIM/HighD/pNEUMA/loop-detector data) or against SUMO ground truth; references are inline literature constants, not reference data files.

NO communication-realism benchmark: no PDR-vs-distance curve, no latency/inter-packet-gap statistics, no CBR-vs-density validation against DSRC/C-V2X field measurements. Radio tests (test_radio_propagation.py) assert only qualitative monotonicity and self-consistency (sigma=0 == disc), never proximity to measured curves. The engine has the ingredients (disc/logdistance+shadowing, packet_loss_base, NLOS, chan_capacity=40 congestion at run.py:341, weather) but their parameters are unvalidated defaults.

The datasheet 'Realism scorecard' (datasheet.py:216-252) uses very wide pass bands (benign speed p95 anywhere in 5-45 m/s passes; attacker prevalence 0.03-0.45) — it is a sanity check, not a realism benchmark; no distribution-level distance (KS/Wasserstein/EMD) against any reference for speed/accel/headway.
Tests assert DIRECTION not MAGNITUDE ('lights lower mean speed by >1 m/s', 'multilane beats single-lane by >1 m/s') — nothing checks that the magnitudes match empirical urban traffic.

No cross-fidelity harness comparing the pure-Python engine against the MOSAIC/SUMO layer (both exist in-repo) or against the third_party VeReMi NextGen outputs — no way to quantify how far mock_pipeline kinematics/comm are from the higher-fidelity stack.

verify_data.py N1 (:443-489) validates road-network structure (indices, counts) only — no network realism metrics (intersection density, block-length distribution, node degree distribution, speed-limit mix vs real OSM cities).

gt_emissions_sample.jsonl is a probabilistic SAMPLE by default (emit_sample_prob<1), so per-vehicle trajectory reconstruction (needed for accel/headway metrics) is lossy unless emit_sample_prob=1.0 is set as tests do (test_gap_acceptance.py:45-48); no dedicated full-trajectory realism output exists.
corpus_report.py measures corpus BALANCE, not realism — 'difficulty spread' is detection recall spread, and 'domain diversity' counts topology labels, not realism of any domain.
opportunities: Create datagen/realism_bench.py mirroring calibration.py's shape (numpy-only, dataset_dir CLI, JSON out): compute benign speed/accel/headway distributions and an edge-level fundamental diagram from ground_truth/gt_emissions_sample.jsonl (fields: t, true_x/true_y, claimed_speed, true_vehicle_id, is_attacker/is_faulty/falsified — per-vehicle finite differencing gives accel; nearest-node/edge assignment gives density-flow bins), and score each with KS/Wasserstein against reference distributions shipped as data files (pNEUMA/NGSIM/HighD summaries). The KS implementation to reuse is calibration._ks_vs_rayleigh (calibration.py:35-42).

Run realism metrics on FULL traces by setting emit_sample_prob=1.0 (already a supported knob, used by test_gap_acceptance._flow_cfg:45-48), or better: attach a collector to the existing digest-neutral telemetry seams run.PER_STEP_HOOK / LANE_CHANGE_HOOK / GAP_YIELD_HOOK (proven side-effect-free on the digest in test_lane_changes.py:149-153 and test_gap_acceptance.py:232-242) so a realism harness observes every step without changing any golden digest.

Comm-realism module: reconstruct heard-distance per report exactly as test_radio_propagation._honest_heard_dists does (dist = detnorm_acceptanceRangeThreshold*art_max + radio_range_m, :58-72) to build empirical PDR-vs-distance curves from ma_reports + gt emissions; compare against published DSRC/ITS-G5 field-measurement curves and against third_party/veremi-nextgen OMNeT++ reference configs (snirThreshold 4dB etc.).

Wire the new realism scores into (a) datasheet.py's Realism scorecard (:216-252) replacing/extending the wide bands, (b) validate.py or a sibling so campaign.py:105 and massive.py:463 record per-domain realism alongside recall, and (c) corpus_report.py's warnings machinery — it already exits nonzero on warnings (corpus_report.py:564-565) so realism regressions become a CI gate for free.
Add a realism validity gate to foundry fitness (foundry.py:196-231 already has the report-activity gate pattern) so evolved scenarios cannot 'win' by being kinematically absurd.

Cross-fidelity harness: run the same scenario spec through mock_pipeline and through scms-sim MOSAIC/SUMO (toolchain at C:/Users/Administrator/tools) and diff the realism-metric vectors — quantifies python-engine fidelity and directly serves the state-of-the-art mission; nothing like it exists today.

Network realism metrics for verify_data.py N1 / osm.py imports: intersection density, block-length and node-degree distributions of network.json vs real OSM references — osm_to_network (mock_pipeline/osm.py, tested in test_osm_import.py) already imports real cities, so the reference is obtainable from the same source.

Benchmark distributional comparability against VeReMi NextGen (third_party/veremi-nextgen holds the dataset generator + docs): compare CAM feature distributions (speed/heading/accel/pos-noise) so the corpus can claim parity with the community-standard misbehavior dataset.

Keep every addition read-only/deterministic and default-OFF, following the repo's iron rule: golden byte-digests (04ae9736f519… family) are pinned in at least four test files and any change to default engine behavior breaks the whole suite.
notes: Bottom line for the mission: roughly 0% of a REALISM benchmark harness exists for traffic and comm — the repo's benchmarking muscle is entirely detection-metric (ROC/PR/recall@FPR/precision-recall of revocation) plus one GNSS-error calibration and a wide-band plausibility scorecard. What DOES exist and is directly reusable: (a) the calibration.py pattern (numpy KS vs a reference model, dataset-dir CLI, JSON output, embedded into datasheet) is the exact template a traffic/comm realism module should follow; (b) full-trace observability already exists via emit_sample_prob=1.0 and three digest-neutral hooks (PER_STEP_HOOK, LANE_CHANGE_HOOK, GAP_YIELD_HOOK in mock_pipeline/run.py); (c) integration points where realism scores would automatically propagate: validate/campaign/massive per-domain metrics, datasheet scorecard, corpus_report CI gate, foundry fitness validity gate; (d) heard-distance reconstruction from detnorm_acceptanceRangeThreshold enables PDR-vs-distance without new engine output. Hard constraint discovered: default-config golden byte-digests are pinned across many test files, so all realism instrumentation must be read-only or default-OFF. The MOSAIC/SUMO layer has zero validation harness; third_party/veremi-nextgen provides reference OMNeT++/MOSAIC configs and a community-standard dataset for comparability benchmarking. Note the third_party/veremi-nextgen submodule is dirty (git status 'm'), untouched by this investigation.
